issues.detail: The Greek 'ων' (genitive plural) refers back to the people who were not worthy, but the Vietnamese 'thế gian không xứng đáng cho họ' implies the world was not worthy *for* them. The Greek 'οὐκ ἦν ἀξιος ὁ κόσμος' means 'the world was not worthy [of them]'. The Vietnamese structure reverses the relationship of worthiness.
The Greek 'τὰς οπαῖς τῆς γῆς' refers to the 'depths of the earth'. The Vietnamese 'hang dưới đất' (caves under the ground) is a specific interpretation that misses the broader concept of 'depths'.
